library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

# Model and source

* Citation: Majid O, Laurenza A, Ferry J, Hussein Z. Impact of perampanel on
  pharmacokinetics of concomitant antiepileptics in patients with
  partial-onset seizures: pooled analysis of clinical trials. Br J Clin
  Pharmacol. 2016;82(2):422-430.
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/bcp.12951> (open access,
  [PMC4972158](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4972158/))
* Supplement: Supporting Information file 1 of the article (Supplemental
  Tables S1-S11, one final model per antiepileptic drug).

Majid 2016 pooled the three Phase III trials of adjunctive perampanel in
refractory partial-onset seizures and fitted one population model per
concomitant antiepileptic drug (AED) to ask whether perampanel changes that
AED's apparent clearance. Eleven AEDs taken by at least 30 patients were
analysed. Ten of the eleven final models are packaged here, one file per
drug, as the authors fitted them independently:

```{r models}
models <- c(
  carbamazepine = "Majid_2016_carbamazepine",
  clobazam      = "Majid_2016_clobazam",
  clonazepam    = "Majid_2016_clonazepam",
  lamotrigine   = "Majid_2016_lamotrigine",
  levetiracetam = "Majid_2016_levetiracetam",
  oxcarbazepine = "Majid_2016_oxcarbazepine",
  phenobarbital = "Majid_2016_phenobarbital",
  topiramate    = "Majid_2016_topiramate",
  valproic_acid = "Majid_2016_valproic_acid",
  zonisamide    = "Majid_2016_zonisamide"
)
uis <- lapply(models, function(nm) rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(nm)))
```

The phenytoin model (Supplemental Table S8) is not packaged; see
[Assumptions and deviations](#assumptions-and-deviations).

# Model structure

The data were sparse (two samples 1-2 h apart at each maintenance visit, one
sample at each baseline visit) and the time of the concomitant AED dose was
not recorded, so no compartmental model could be fitted. Each observed
concentration was instead treated as an average steady-state concentration
(Majid 2016 Methods, PK model and parameters):

$$C_{av,ss} = \frac{R_0}{CL/F}, \qquad R_0 = \frac{\text{total daily dose}}{24\ \text{h}}$$

The packaged models are therefore algebraic: there is no volume, no
absorption and no dosing record. The AED's own daily dose is supplied as a
covariate column (`DOSE_<AED>_MGD`), and `Cc` is the predicted steady-state
concentration. Between-subject variability on CL/F is exponential, and
inter-occasion variability (IOV) is defined on five identical occasions:
visits 1 and 2 (before perampanel) and visits 6, 7 and 8 (maintenance weeks
10, 14 and 19), encoded as `OCC` = 1-5.

The paper does not print the covariate equations. The form used for every
model is

$$CL/F = \theta_{basal} \cdot \left(1 + \sum_k \theta_k X_k\right) \cdot e^{\eta_{CL} + \kappa_{CL,occ}}$$

with binary indicators entering as $X_k \in \{0, 1\}$ and body weight as the
uncentred ratio `WT / 70`. Carbamazepine adds an absolute dose term to the
basal clearance. The [form-deduction section](#deducing-the-covariate-form-from-table-2)
shows how Table 2 and Figure 1 select this form over the alternatives.

# Population

```{r population}
pop <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(uis), function(d) {
  p <- uis[[d]]$population
  data.frame(
    AED = d,
    n = p$n_subjects,
    `Mean age (SD), y` = sub("SD ", "", sub("^mean ", "", sub(" years$", "", p$age_median))),
    `Mean weight (SD), kg` = sub("SD ", "", sub("^mean ", "", sub(" kg$", "", p$weight_median))),
    `Female, %` = p$sex_female_pct,
    `White, %` = unname(p$race_ethnicity["White"]),
    `Asian incl. Chinese, %` = unname(p$race_ethnicity["Asian"] + p$race_ethnicity["Chinese"]),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}))
knitr::kable(pop, caption = "Demographics by concomitant AED (Majid 2016 Table 1). Patients could take up to three AEDs, so the groups overlap.")
```

Patients were aged 12 years or older with partial-onset seizures
uncontrolled despite at least two AEDs in the previous two years, and could
take up to three stable concomitant AEDs (at most one enzyme inducer) plus
perampanel 2-12 mg or placebo once daily at bedtime. The AED doses were not
reported. The same information is available programmatically through each
model's `population` element, e.g.
`rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Majid_2016_valproic_acid"))$population`.

# Source trace

Every value comes from the final-model table of the Supplement for that
drug, column "Final estimate". The in-file comment on each `ini()` line
quotes the table row.

```{r source-trace}
# Values transcribed from the Supplement, in the order the tables print
# them. The basal clearance is stored as lcl = log(value); IIV and IOV are
# variances; the residual 'proportional' row is a variance (see
# Assumptions), so propSd = sqrt(value).
published <- list(
  carbamazepine = list(table = "S1", basal = 0.375, effects = c(e_dose_cbz_cl = 0.00347, e_conmed_vpa_cl = 0.125, e_dose_perampanel_cl = 0.00357), iiv = 0.0512, iov = 0.0246, prop = 0.0167),
  clobazam      = list(table = "S2", basal = 4.76,  effects = c(e_sexf_cl = -0.387, e_wt_cl = -0.312, e_conmed_pht_cl = 0.545, e_cp_perampanel_cl = 0.0000678), iiv = 0.497, iov = 0.0258, prop = 0.059),
  clonazepam    = list(table = "S3", basal = 2.53,  effects = c(e_conmed_pht_cl = 1.89, e_conmed_vpa_cl = 0.785, e_conmed_clb_cl = 1.01), iiv = 0.388, iov = 0.0513, prop = 0.0171),
  lamotrigine   = list(table = "S4", basal = 1.18,  effects = c(e_conmed_cbz_cl = 0.584, e_conmed_pb_cl = 0.742, e_conmed_vpa_cl = -0.51, e_dose_perampanel_cl = 0.037), iiv = 0.249, iov = 0.0296, prop = 0.0193),
  levetiracetam = list(table = "S5", basal = 2.28,  effects = c(e_sexf_cl = -0.244, e_wt_cl = 0.389, e_conmed_pht_cl = -0.252, e_conmed_vpa_cl = -0.154), iiv = 0.23, iov = 0.034, prop = 0.0717),
  oxcarbazepine = list(table = "S6", basal = 63.4,  effects = c(e_sexf_cl = -0.263, e_conmed_pht_cl = 0.823, e_conmed_perampanel_cl = -0.261), iiv = 0.305, iov = 0.195, prop = 0.407),
  phenobarbital = list(table = "S7", basal = 0.243, effects = c(e_transaminase_gt2uln_cl = 0.24, e_conmed_lamotrigine_cl = -0.24, e_conmed_oxc_cl = -0.325), iiv = 0.281, iov = 0.0189, prop = 0.0112),
  topiramate    = list(table = "S9", basal = 0.953, effects = c(e_wt_cl = 0.878, e_conmed_pht_cl = 0.714, e_conmed_zns_cl = 1.12), iiv = 0.212, iov = 0.0292, prop = 0.0278),
  valproic_acid = list(table = "S10", basal = 0.401, effects = c(e_wt_cl = 0.490, e_dose_perampanel_cl = 0.00761), iiv = 0.316, iov = 0.0308, prop = 0.0259),
  zonisamide    = list(table = "S11", basal = 0.558, effects = c(e_conmed_pht_cl = 0.581, e_conmed_pb_cl = 0.491, e_conmed_clb_cl = -0.334), iiv = 0.235, iov = 0.0216, prop = 0.0141)
)

trace <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(published), function(d) {
  p <- published[[d]]
  ui <- uis[[d]]
  th <- ui$theta
  om <- diag(ui$omega)
  # Every theta in the model must be one the table prints, and vice versa.
  stopifnot(setequal(names(th), c("lcl", names(p$effects), "propSd")))
  stopifnot(
    abs(exp(th[["lcl"]]) - p$basal) < 1e-9,
    all(abs(th[names(p$effects)] - p$effects) < 1e-12),
    abs(om[["etalcl"]] - p$iiv) < 1e-12,
    all(abs(om[paste0("etaiov_cl_", 1:5)] - p$iov) < 1e-12),
    abs(th[["propSd"]] - sqrt(p$prop)) < 5e-4
  )
  data.frame(
    AED = d,
    Table = p$table,
    `Basal CL/F (L/h)` = p$basal,
    `Covariate effects` = paste(sprintf("%s = %s", names(p$effects), signif(p$effects, 3)), collapse = "; "),
    `IIV / IOV variance` = sprintf("%s / %s", p$iiv, p$iov),
    `Residual variance -> propSd` = sprintf("%s -> %.4f", p$prop, sqrt(p$prop)),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}))
knitr::kable(trace, caption = "Final estimates transcribed from Majid 2016 Supplemental Tables S1-S11 (phenytoin, Table S8, excluded). Each row is asserted against the packaged model.")
```

| Equation | Source location |
|----------|-----------------|
| `Cc = (DOSE / 24) / cl` | Majid 2016 Methods, PK model and parameters (C_av,ss = R0 / CL) |
| Exponential IIV on CL/F | Methods ("estimated using an exponential model") |
| IOV on five identical occasions (visits 1, 2, 6, 7, 8) | Methods |
| Proportional residual error | Supplemental Tables S1-S11 (only a proportional row is printed) |
| Relative-additive covariate bracket, uncentred `WT / 70` | Not printed; deduced from Table 2 (next section) |
| Carbamazepine absolute dose term | Not printed; deduced from Table 2 and Figure 1A (next section) |
| Lamotrigine `ln(perampanel dose)` term | Table S4 row label and Results ("proportionally to the loge of perampanel daily dose") |

# Deducing the covariate form from Table 2

Table 2 of the paper prints the model-predicted typical CL/F of each AED
without perampanel and with 8 and 12 mg perampanel, for the subgroups each
final model distinguishes. Those numbers are produced by the unprinted
covariate equations, so they test candidate forms. The helper below returns
the typical-value clearance of a packaged model for given covariates.

```{r typical-helper}
# Typical-value solve: one row per covariate combination, all random
# effects zeroed. The models are algebraic, so a single observation row per
# subject is enough.
typical <- function(ui, covs) {
  ev <- covs
  ev$id <- seq_len(nrow(ev))
  ev$time <- 0
  ev$evid <- 0
  if (is.null(ev$OCC)) ev$OCC <- 1
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui), ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  if (is.null(out$id)) out$id <- 1L
  stopifnot(nrow(out) == nrow(covs))
  out
}

# A printed value p with `dp` decimals is reproduced when the model value
# lies within half a unit of the last printed digit, widened by 0.15% for
# the rounding of the three-significant-figure parameter estimates.
reproduces <- function(model, printed, dp) {
  abs(model - printed) <= 0.5 * 10^(-dp) + 0.0015 * printed
}
```

```{r table2}
dose_rows <- data.frame(per_mg = c(0, 8, 12))
per3 <- c("without", "8 mg", "12 mg")

t2_cbz <- typical(uis$carbamazepine, data.frame(
  DOSE_CBZ_MGD = 900, CONMED_VPA = 0, DOSE_PERAMPANEL_MGD = dose_rows$per_mg
)) |> mutate(AED = "CBZ", group = "all", perampanel = per3, printed = c(3.50, 3.60, 3.65), dp = 2)

t2_ltg <- typical(uis$lamotrigine, data.frame(
  DOSE_LTG_MGD = 200, CONMED_CBZ = 0, CONMED_PB = 0, CONMED_VPA = 0,
  DOSE_PERAMPANEL_MGD = dose_rows$per_mg
)) |> mutate(AED = "LTG", group = "all", perampanel = per3, printed = c(1.18, 1.27, 1.29), dp = 2)

t2_vpa <- typical(uis$valproic_acid, data.frame(
  DOSE_VPA_MGD = 1000, WT = 70, DOSE_PERAMPANEL_MGD = dose_rows$per_mg
)) |> mutate(AED = "VPA", group = "all", perampanel = per3, printed = c(0.60, 0.62, 0.63), dp = 2)

# Clobazam's perampanel term is per ng/mL of perampanel. The perampanel
# concentrations behind Table 2 are not printed; 0 / 270 / 330 ng/mL lie in
# the windows that reproduce BOTH sexes (derived below).
t2_clb <- typical(uis$clobazam, data.frame(
  DOSE_CLB_MGD = 20, WT = 70, CONMED_PHT = 0,
  SEXF = rep(c(0, 1), each = 3),
  CP_PERAMPANEL_NGML = rep(c(0, 270, 330), 2)
)) |> mutate(AED = "CLB", group = rep(c("males", "females"), each = 3),
             perampanel = rep(c("without", "8 mg (270 ng/mL)", "12 mg (330 ng/mL)"), 2),
             printed = c(3.27, 3.36, 3.38, 1.43, 1.52, 1.54), dp = 2)

t2_oxc <- typical(uis$oxcarbazepine, data.frame(
  DOSE_OXC_MGD = 1200,
  SEXF = c(0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 1),
  CONMED_PHT = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1),
  CONMED_PERAMPANEL = c(0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1)
)) |> mutate(AED = "OXC", perampanel = rep(c("without", "with"), 4),
             group = rep(c("males, no PHT", "females, no PHT", "males, PHT", "females, PHT"), each = 2),
             printed = c(63.4, 46.9, 46.7, 30.2, 115.6, 98.9, 99.0, 82.4), dp = 1)

t2 <- dplyr::bind_rows(t2_cbz, t2_ltg, t2_vpa, t2_clb, t2_oxc) |>
  mutate(ok = reproduces(tvcl, printed, dp))

t2 |>
  select(AED, group, perampanel, printed, tvcl, ok) |>
  rename(`Table 2 CL/F (L/h)` = printed, `Model CL/F (L/h)` = tvcl,
         Reproduced = ok) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Typical CL/F from the packaged models against Majid 2016 Table 2.")

stopifnot(nrow(t2) == 23, all(t2$ok))
```

All 23 printed cells are reproduced. What each block establishes:

* **Oxcarbazepine** (8 cells, all covariates binary): every effect is
  additive inside one relative bracket. Females without phenytoin lose
  0.263 x 63.4 = 16.7 L/h and perampanel subtracts the same 16.5 L/h in
  every subgroup. This is why Table 3 reports different relative
  reductions (26%, 35.3%, 14.4%, 16.8%) for one perampanel coefficient.
  A multiplicative form (`exp(theta)` or `(1 + theta)` per covariate) gives
  63.4 x 0.769 = 48.7 L/h for females and cannot reproduce the table.
* **Clobazam**: going from 4.76 L/h (basal) to 3.27 L/h for males requires
  the weight term to contribute -0.312 x 1.003, which is the uncentred
  `WT / WTref` at the reference weight. A power `(WT / 70)^-0.312` or a
  centred linear term gives 4.76 L/h there. Females then follow with no
  further freedom: 4.76 x (1 - 0.387 - 0.312) = 1.433 L/h, printed 1.43.
  The perampanel increment is the same in both sexes (+0.09 / +0.11 L/h),
  so it too sits inside the bracket, as the paper says ("proportional to
  perampanel concentrations and to clobazam clearance").
* **Valproic acid**: the same uncentred weight term,
  0.401 x (1 + 0.490) = 0.597 L/h, printed 0.60. With perampanel inside the
  same bracket the cells are 0.622 and 0.634 (printed 0.62, 0.63). If
  perampanel multiplied separately the 8 mg cell would be 0.634, printed
  0.62. The paper's "5.0% at 12 mg" is 0.63 / 0.60 of the rounded cells.
* **Lamotrigine**: 1.18 x (1 + 0.037 ln 8) = 1.271 and
  1.18 x (1 + 0.037 ln 12) = 1.289 L/h.
* **Carbamazepine**: the cells need a carbamazepine dose. 3.50 L/h
  back-solves to 900 mg/day under the absolute dose term used here, a
  typical maintenance dose. The perampanel cells then follow at
  +2.9% / +4.3%.

```{r clobazam-window}
# The perampanel concentration that reproduces a printed clobazam cell is a
# window; the additive form must find ONE concentration per dose level that
# satisfies males and females at once.
k <- exp(uis$clobazam$theta[["lcl"]]) * uis$clobazam$theta[["e_cp_perampanel_cl"]]
base <- t2_clb$tvcl[c(1, 4)] # males, females without perampanel
window <- function(printed, base) (printed + c(-0.005, 0.005) - base) / k
w8 <- rbind(window(3.36, base[1]), window(1.52, base[2]))
w12 <- rbind(window(3.38, base[1]), window(1.54, base[2]))
cp8 <- c(max(w8[, 1]), min(w8[, 2]))
cp12 <- c(max(w12[, 1]), min(w12[, 2]))
cp8
cp12
stopifnot(cp8[1] < cp8[2], cp12[1] < cp12[2])

# A perampanel factor multiplying the whole clearance would need ONE ratio
# for both sexes; the windows do not overlap.
ratio <- function(printed, base) (printed + c(-0.005, 0.005)) / base
r12 <- rbind(ratio(3.38, base[1]), ratio(1.54, base[2]))
r12
stopifnot(max(r12[, 1]) > min(r12[, 2]))
```

The implied perampanel concentrations, about 255-279 ng/mL at 8 mg and
317-341 ng/mL at 12 mg, are plausible for a cohort in which many patients
took enzyme-inducing AEDs that lower perampanel exposure.

## Carbamazepine dose term: Figure 1A

Three forms of the carbamazepine dose effect are compatible with the
printed coefficient: an absolute term
`CL = 0.375 + 0.00347 * DOSE` (used here), a relative term
`CL = 0.375 * (1 + 0.00347 * DOSE)`, and an exponential
`CL = 0.375 * exp(0.00347 * DOSE)`. Table 2's 3.50 L/h requires 900,
2400 and 643 mg/day respectively. Figure 1A shows a carbamazepine median
of about 10 ug/mL, flat across visits, with the interquartile range
roughly 8-12 ug/mL.

```{r cbz-forms}
cbz_dose <- c(400, 600, 800, 1000, 1200, 1600)
cbz_forms <- data.frame(dose = cbz_dose) |>
  mutate(
    absolute = (dose / 24) / (0.375 + 0.00347 * dose),
    relative = (dose / 24) / (0.375 * (1 + 0.00347 * dose)),
    exponential = (dose / 24) / (0.375 * exp(0.00347 * dose))
  )
# The packaged model must equal the absolute form.
pkg <- typical(uis$carbamazepine, data.frame(
  DOSE_CBZ_MGD = cbz_dose, CONMED_VPA = 0, DOSE_PERAMPANEL_MGD = 0
))
stopifnot(all(abs(pkg$Cc - cbz_forms$absolute) < 1e-9))

cbz_forms |>
  rename(`CBZ dose (mg/day)` = dose,
         `Absolute (packaged)` = absolute,
         `Relative` = relative,
         `Exponential` = exponential) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Typical carbamazepine Css (ug/mL), no valproic acid, no perampanel, under the three candidate dose forms.")

# Over the usual 600-1200 mg/day maintenance range the packaged form stays
# inside Figure 1A's interquartile range; the relative form sits above the
# upper whisker (about 18 ug/mL) and the exponential form collapses with dose.
mid <- cbz_forms$dose >= 600 & cbz_forms$dose <= 1200
stopifnot(
  all(cbz_forms$absolute[mid] > 8 & cbz_forms$absolute[mid] < 12),
  all(cbz_forms$relative[mid] > 18),
  cbz_forms$exponential[cbz_forms$dose == 1200] < 3
)
```

The absolute form also behaves like carbamazepine autoinduction:
concentration approaches the ceiling 1 / (24 x 0.00347) = 12.0 ug/mL as the
dose rises.

# Typical concentrations against Figure 1

The paper reports no AED doses, so its box plots (Figure 1) cannot be
re-simulated. What can be checked is that each model, at an ordinary
adult maintenance dose and with no interacting co-medication, predicts a
concentration of the same order as Figure 1's median. This catches unit
errors (ng/mL against ug/mL) and gross structural errors. The doses below
are assumptions, not values from the paper; the medians were read from
Figure 1 by the maintainers.

```{r figure1-typical}
fig1 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~AED,            ~dose, ~fig1_median, ~unit,
  "carbamazepine",   800,     10,       "ug/mL",
  "clobazam",         20,    250,       "ng/mL",
  "clonazepam",        2,     20,       "ng/mL",
  "lamotrigine",     300,      7.5,     "ug/mL",
  "levetiracetam",  2000,     28,       "ug/mL",
  "oxcarbazepine",  1200,      0.7,     "ug/mL",
  "phenobarbital",   150,     25,       "ug/mL",
  "topiramate",      300,      7.5,     "ug/mL",
  "valproic_acid",  1250,     80,       "ug/mL",
  "zonisamide",      300,     17,       "ug/mL"
)

# Reference covariates: 70 kg male, no interacting co-medication, no
# perampanel, normal transaminases.
ref_covs <- function(aed, dose) {
  base <- data.frame(WT = 70, SEXF = 0, CONMED_PHT = 0, CONMED_VPA = 0,
                     CONMED_CLB = 0, CONMED_CBZ = 0, CONMED_PB = 0,
                     CONMED_LAMOTRIGINE = 0, CONMED_OXC = 0, CONMED_ZNS = 0,
                     CONMED_PERAMPANEL = 0, DOSE_PERAMPANEL_MGD = 0,
                     CP_PERAMPANEL_NGML = 0, TRANSAMINASE_GT2ULN = 0)
  dose_col <- c(carbamazepine = "DOSE_CBZ_MGD", clobazam = "DOSE_CLB_MGD",
                clonazepam = "DOSE_CZP_MGD", lamotrigine = "DOSE_LTG_MGD",
                levetiracetam = "DOSE_LEV_MGD", oxcarbazepine = "DOSE_OXC_MGD",
                phenobarbital = "DOSE_PB_MGD", topiramate = "DOSE_TPM_MGD",
                valproic_acid = "DOSE_VPA_MGD", zonisamide = "DOSE_ZNS_MGD")[[aed]]
  base[[dose_col]] <- dose
  base
}

fig1$model <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(fig1)), function(i) {
  typical(uis[[fig1$AED[i]]], ref_covs(fig1$AED[i], fig1$dose[i]))$Cc
}, numeric(1))
fig1$ratio <- fig1$model / fig1$fig1_median

fig1 |>
  rename(`Assumed dose (mg/day)` = dose, `Figure 1 median` = fig1_median,
         Unit = unit, `Model typical Css` = model, `Model / Figure 1` = ratio) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Typical steady-state concentration at an assumed maintenance dose against the Figure 1 median.")

stopifnot(all(fig1$ratio > 0.5 & fig1$ratio < 2))
```

# Simulation: oxcarbazepine by visit

The oxcarbazepine model carries the only perampanel effect the paper
considered potentially relevant. The simulation below mirrors the study
design: visits 1 and 2 before perampanel, visits 6-8 on maintenance, half
the cohort on perampanel and half on placebo, with between-subject and
inter-occasion variability. Doses (600-2400 mg/day) and covariates are
assumptions; 49% male and 6.5% on phenytoin follow Tables 1 and 2.

```{r oxc-sim}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2016)
set.seed(2016)
n_arm <- 200
subj <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(2 * n_arm),
  arm = rep(c("perampanel", "placebo"), each = n_arm),
  SEXF = rbinom(2 * n_arm, 1, 0.51),
  CONMED_PHT = rbinom(2 * n_arm, 1, 0.065),
  DOSE_OXC_MGD = sample(c(600, 900, 1200, 1500, 1800, 2400), 2 * n_arm, replace = TRUE)
)
visits <- data.frame(OCC = 1:5, visit = factor(c("Baseline 1", "Baseline 2", "6", "7", "8"),
                                               levels = c("Baseline 1", "Baseline 2", "6", "7", "8")))
ev <- merge(subj, visits) |>
  arrange(id, OCC) |>
  mutate(
    time = (OCC - 1) * 24 * 7,
    evid = 0,
    CONMED_PERAMPANEL = as.integer(arm == "perampanel" & OCC >= 3)
  )
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(uis$oxcarbazepine, ev, returnType = "data.frame",
                       keep = c("arm", "visit", "CONMED_PERAMPANEL"))

ggplot(sim, aes(visit, sim, fill = arm)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 4)) +
  labs(x = "Visit", y = "Oxcarbazepine (ug/mL)", fill = NULL,
       title = "Simulated oxcarbazepine concentration by visit",
       caption = "Compare Majid 2016 Figure 1F (perampanel-treated patients only).") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r oxc-check}
pre_post <- sim |>
  filter(arm == "perampanel") |>
  mutate(phase = ifelse(CONMED_PERAMPANEL == 1, "on", "pre")) |>
  group_by(phase) |>
  summarise(median = median(sim), .groups = "drop")
pre_post
ratio_on_pre <- pre_post$median[pre_post$phase == "on"] / pre_post$median[pre_post$phase == "pre"]
ratio_on_pre
# Typical-value ratio is 1 / (1 - 0.261 / bracket), 1.35 (males) to 1.55
# (females) without phenytoin. The pooled-observation median carries the
# large IOV and residual variance of this model, so the bound is wide
# (about 4 standard errors either side of the expected ~1.4); a perampanel
# effect of the wrong sign or of 0 fails it.
stopifnot(ratio_on_pre > 1.1, ratio_on_pre < 1.9)
```

The observed medians in Figure 1F rise only slightly once perampanel
starts (from roughly 0.6 ug/mL at the baseline visits to 0.6-0.7 ug/mL at
visits 6-8), less than the 35-55% rise the 26% clearance reduction implies
at the typical value.
The final oxcarbazepine model also over-predicted low concentrations in
its goodness-of-fit plots (Supplement), and the parent drug, with a short
half-life, is a poor fit to a steady-state assumption when sampling time is
unknown. The model is reproduced as published.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Covariate equations are not printed.** The relative-additive bracket,
  the uncentred `WT / 70` weight term and the absolute carbamazepine dose
  term were deduced from Table 2 and Figure 1 as shown above. Oxcarbazepine,
  clobazam, valproic acid and lamotrigine reproduce Table 2 exactly; the
  levetiracetam and topiramate weight terms and the clonazepam,
  phenobarbital and zonisamide indicators have no Table 2 cell and use the
  same form by analogy, since one analyst fitted all models. For the three
  indicator-only models the Results text fixes the sign of every effect,
  which excludes reading the coefficients as multiplicative factors (the
  clonazepam valproic-acid coefficient 0.785 is an increase).
* **Reference weight.** The weight term needs `WT / WTref = 1` at the
  Table 2 typical value; the reference itself is not printed and 70 kg is
  used.
* **Carbamazepine valproic-acid term.** Its placement (in the relative
  bracket that multiplies the dose-dependent clearance) is not
  identifiable from the published numbers; Table 2 has no valproic-acid
  cell.
* **Perampanel concentration unit (clobazam).** Not printed; ng/mL is
  assumed. The implied concentrations behind Table 2 (about 270 and
  330 ng/mL) are plausible.
* **Lamotrigine at 0 mg perampanel.** The `ln(dose)` term is undefined at
  0 mg; the model uses `ln(max(dose, 1))`, which is 0 for placebo and the
  exact logarithm for every studied dose (2-12 mg).
* **Residual error is read as a variance.** Each supplemental table
  prints the residual "proportional" row in the same "Final estimate"
  column as the IIV and IOV variances, whose %CV is the square root in every
  table. For carbamazepine (0.0167, 12.9%) and zonisamide (0.0141, 11.9%) the
  printed %CV is also the square root; for the other drugs it is 100 times
  the estimate (for example lamotrigine 0.0193, "1.9%"), which would make
  the residual error of a sparse clinical assay 1-3%. `propSd` is
  therefore `sqrt(estimate)` for every model.
* **Additive residual components.** The Supplement says a combined
  proportional and additive error was used for most drugs, but only the
  proportional row is printed. Only proportional error is packaged.
* **Clonazepam Table S3 copy errors.** The SEE, 95% CI and %CV columns of
  Table S3 repeat Table S2 (clobazam) verbatim, including a 95% CI of
  3.041-6.479 around an estimate of 2.53, and Table 2 repeats the clobazam
  IIV/IOV %CV (70.5 / 16.1). The estimates themselves differ from Table S2
  and are used; the implied %CVs are 62.3 (IIV) and 22.6 (IOV).
* **Oxcarbazepine IOV.** The Results give 41% where Table S6 and Table 2
  give 44.2%; the variance 0.195 (sqrt = 44.2%) is used.
* **Phenytoin not packaged.** The Methods state that phenytoin was fitted
  with a Michaelis-Menten model (Vmax, Km) and the Results that its
  clearance rose with its own daily dose, but Table S8 prints only a
  "Phenytoin clearance" of 0.129 L/h with oxcarbazepine and zonisamide
  effects: no Vmax, no Km and no dose term. Read as `Css = R0 / CL`, 0.129
  L/h gives about 97 ug/mL at 300 mg/day against Figure 1H's median of
  about 15 ug/mL. The published parameters do not define a usable model.
* **Bioavailability.** All clearances are apparent (CL/F); F is not
  separable from CL in these data.
* **Bracket positivity.** The clobazam bracket
  `1 - 0.387 SEXF - 0.312 WT/70 + ...` reaches zero for a female heavier
  than about 137 kg, outside the cohort (mean 67.9, SD 17.3 kg).
* **Errata.** A EuropePMC search (2026-11-24) found no erratum or
  correction for this article.
